game: Grand Theft Auto VI — PlayStation 5 trophy list

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: This is the platinum itself, the cover stamp of the whole atlas: it arrives by itself once the other 54 markers are collected, so never chase it directly. PowerPyx frames the full journey as a 4/10-difficulty, roughly 200-hour route that fits inside one playthrough and contains no online trophies at all. Travel the six roadmap stages in order, keep the missable flag in sight during Chapter 1, and this stamp closes the atlas on its own.
steps: Work roadmap stages I–VI in order.
Earn all 54 other trophies.
The platinum unlocks automatically with the last one.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: The first marker on the chart and one nobody can walk past: start the game and play the opening mission, Gone Fishing, all the way to its end card. PSNProfiles catalogues it as a hidden story trophy. There is nothing to prepare and nothing to collect — just finish the mission instead of quitting out of it.
steps: Start a new game.
Play Gone Fishing to its final objective.
Wait for the mission-complete screen; the trophy lands there.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Close out every mission of Chapter 1 and this chapter marker is stamped. PowerPyx budgets the five-chapter story at about 60–80 hours, so this first chapter is only the coastline of a much longer chart. One habit starts here and protects the whole run: drop a manual save when the chapter opens, because the game's single missable trophy takes its first step at Jason's house inside this chapter.
steps: Make a manual save as Chapter 1 begins.
Meditate at Jason's house before the chapter ends (see Positive Mental Attitude).
Finish the chapter's missions through to its end card.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Another unmissable chapter stamp, spelled on the official list with its asterisks exactly as PlayStation publishes it. Exophase's listing ties it simply to finishing Chapter 2, so keep following the story markers: every mission of the chapter, in order, until the chapter closes. No side condition hides behind this one.
steps: Continue the story into Chapter 2.
Complete each of the chapter's missions.
The trophy pops as the chapter ends.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: The Chapter 3 stamp, midway up the rising route. PowerPyx's roadmap treats the chapter trophies as automatic story progress, and this one is no exception: play Chapter 3 from its first mission to its last and the marker fills in. Keep the manual-save-per-chapter habit going — it costs seconds and insures the whole chart.
steps: Save manually at the start of Chapter 3.
Play the chapter's missions in order.
Finish the chapter finale to earn the trophy.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4's completion stamp, listed by PSNProfiles among the hidden story trophies. Like the chapters before it, this one asks for nothing but the story itself: work through every Chapter 4 mission and it unlocks at the chapter's end. After this marker only the finale chapter remains on the story spine.
steps: Enter Chapter 4 with a fresh manual save.
Complete all of its missions.
The trophy unlocks at the chapter's close.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: One of only two golds in the atlas, paid for finishing the story's final mission. PowerPyx's roadmap places it at the end of the five-chapter campaign; free-roam continues after the credits, so nothing else on the chart has to be finished first. Go in with full health, armour and ammo, play the finale to the last objective, and the gold is stamped as the story closes.
steps: Finish Chapters 1–4 and reach the final mission.
Stock up on health, armour and ammunition beforehand.
Complete the final mission through the credits.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: A named-mission stamp from the opening stretch of the story: complete the mission Breakfast Run. GTABase's mission index places it on the Chapter 1 route, so it arrives naturally as you travel stage I — accept the mission when it is offered and play it to its results screen rather than abandoning it mid-way.
steps: Reach the Breakfast Run mission in Chapter 1.
Play it from the opening objective to the end.
The trophy unlocks on the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The stamp for the story's big set-piece robbery, The Cartel Heist. PowerPyx walks this mission inside the main story route, which means no special setup beyond arriving at it: follow the story into stage II, take the heist from briefing to getaway, and the trophy is paid when the mission completes. Failing an objective only costs a restart of that section, never the trophy.
steps: Progress the story until The Cartel Heist begins.
Play the heist through its escape objective.
Finish the mission to stamp the trophy.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play and this marker is yours. PSNProfiles files it with the hidden story set, earned on the stage II route as the campaign moves through Chapters 3–4. As with every named-mission trophy in this atlas, the only requirement is finishing the mission itself — no medal rank or optional objective is attached.
steps: Reach the Child's Play mission in the story.
Complete it from start to finish.
The trophy pops at the results screen.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Exophase ties this stamp to one named job: finish the mission Headliners. It sits on the stage II stretch of the route, inside the middle chapters, and unlocks the moment that mission's final objective resolves. Nothing collectible or timed is involved — arrive, play it through, move on.
steps: Advance the story to the Headliners mission.
Complete every objective of the mission.
The trophy unlocks as the mission ends.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: The VCIA Takedown mission carries this stamp. GTABase's mission listing places it among the mid-story jobs of stage II, so the route is simple: keep travelling the story spine until the takedown is offered, then finish it in one sitting. The trophy is paid on completion, whatever approach you take inside the mission.
steps: Reach VCIA Takedown on the story route.
Play the mission to its final objective.
Completion stamps the trophy.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Finish Operation Savage Glory, the last of the named set-piece missions on the stage II route, and this stamp joins the chart. PowerPyx counts it among the automatic story trophies: no optional condition, no medal target — the mission's own completion is the whole requirement. It is a good moment to refresh your per-chapter manual save before stage III opens the strand country.
steps: Progress to Operation Savage Glory in the story.
Complete the operation's objectives in order.
The trophy unlocks at mission end.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold, and the atlas's longest road: push the game's own completion counter to a full 100%. PowerPyx's roadmap treats this as the sum of everything else on the chart — story, strands, activities, collectibles and exploration all feed the percentage. Work it last, in stage VI, using the in-game completion checklist to find whatever slice is still missing rather than guessing.
steps: Finish the story and all side strands.
Clear the activities and collectible sets the counter tracks.
Check the in-game 100% list for stragglers and close them out.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: A silver paid in landings: complete 250 stunts scattered across the whole state. PowerPyx's approach to count trophies like this one is to spread them over the entire playthrough instead of farming at the end — every ramp you pass on story business is one more stamp. A light car or a fast bike forgives most landing angles; a stunt only counts when the landing is clean.
steps: Take every stunt spot you pass while travelling.
Keep rough per-region tallies so no cluster is skipped.
Reach 250 completed stunts.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: The atlas's sampler plate: try every distinct activity type in the game at least once. GTABase's activity index is the checklist to work against — races, the shooting range, fishing, arcade cabinets, drone racing and the rest. Winning is never required, only a genuine attempt, so clear this early in stage IV and learn which activities the harder trophies will ask you to master.
steps: List every activity type as it unlocks on the map.
Play one round or event of each type.
Stop when no untouched activity type remains.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold medals on every Shooting Range challenge — 42 challenges by the published count. PowerPyx's medal discipline applies cleanly here: spend practice runs learning each challenge's target rhythm, then value accuracy over raw speed, because missed shots cost more than a patient trigger. Every challenge can be retried as often as needed, so nothing about this silver can be missed.
steps: Unlock the range and its full challenge list.
Practise each challenge until its pattern is familiar.
Post gold-medal scores on all 42 challenges.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Not participation — victory: win a Top Fun drone race at every race location on the map. PSNProfiles states the requirement per location, so tick venues off as your route crosses them and never leave a region with its race unwon. A slow sighting lap first teaches the gate order; the flying lap afterwards is where the win comes from.
steps: Find every Top Fun drone race location.
Run one practice lap to learn each course.
Win the race at every location.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Twenty race wins, and the word that matters is different: Exophase's listing matches the official text, and repeating one easy circuit twenty times builds nothing. Spread the wins across venues and categories as they unlock, and keep your vehicle upgraded so the later fields stay beatable instead of turning into a wall at win fifteen.
steps: Enter races across different categories and venues.
After each win, move to a race you have not won.
Reach 20 distinct race victories.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal head-to-head in his fishing challenge: when the timer ends, your catch is weighed against his. GTABase files fishing among the repeatable pastimes, and the steady play wins this one — bring the best rod and bait you have unlocked, fish the marked water, and bank reliable mid-size catches instead of gambling the whole round on a single trophy fish.
steps: Unlock fishing and accept Cal's challenge marker.
Equip your best rod and bait.
Finish with a heavier total catch than Cal.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: The cheapest stamp in the fairgrounds: complete one full game on any arcade cabinet. PSNProfiles lists no score condition at all — completion is the whole bar — so choose the shortest cabinet game available, play it through to its end screen, and walk away with the trophy.
steps: Enter an arcade and pick a cabinet.
Play the game through to its end screen.
Leave the cabinet once completion registers.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's side strand at its final mission. Strands surface in free roam between story beats, and PowerPyx's roadmap gives them a stage of their own because finished strands also feed the Strangers & Freaks silver. Follow Andy's markers in the order they appear; the bronze is paid only by the strand's last mission, not by the earlier ones.
steps: Start Andy's strand from his map marker.
Complete his missions in order.
Finish his final mission.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's strand, closed at its final mission. GTABase indexes this arc among the side-character strands that open as the map expands in stage III. The missions chain from his first marker, so the whole job is simply to keep returning until the chain runs out — the last link pays the trophy.
steps: Find Kenton's first marker and open the strand.
Complete his missions as they unlock.
Finish the final Kenton mission.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand final. PSNProfiles carries it as a hidden bronze like the other strand endings, and it counts double on the chart: toward its own stamp and toward the eight finished strands the Strangers & Freaks silver demands. Strands are short — clearing Billy's whenever your route crosses his territory keeps the stage VI cleanup lean.
steps: Start Billy's strand from his marker.
Work through the strand's mission chain.
Complete his final mission.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: The silver that organises stage III: bring eight complete stranger strands to their final missions, anywhere in Leonida. Five of the eight are already on this chart with bronzes of their own — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — so those five plus any three more strands close the count. PowerPyx counts a strand only at its final mission; half-finished arcs pay nothing here.
steps: Finish the five named strands: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone.
Hunt three further stranger markers across the state.
Complete each strand's final mission until eight are done.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand, finished at its last mission. Exophase lists Supply & Demand as a hidden bronze strand final, and like every named strand in stage III it also advances the eight-strand count behind Strangers & Freaks. Work the chain in order and do not leave it one mission short — only the finale pays.
steps: Open Randy's strand from his marker.
Complete his missions in sequence.
Finish the final mission for Randy.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Close Tyrone's strand with his final mission, the last of the five named strand finals on the stage III route. GTABase groups it with the other side-character endings; the pattern is the same as its neighbours — markers chain in order, and the trophy is awarded at the very end of the chain and nowhere earlier.
steps: Pick up Tyrone's strand marker.
Complete the strand's missions in order.
Finish his final mission.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: ⚑ THE one missable trophy on this chart — the red flag of the atlas. Meditate at every meditation spot in Leonida, and understand the trap before anything else: PowerPyx warns that the spot at Jason's house can only be used during Chapter 1, before that chapter ends; sail past it and no later save repairs the run short of starting over. Meditate there at the first opportunity, keep a Chapter 1 manual save as insurance, then sweep the remaining spots in free roam whenever you like — those stay open all game.
steps: During Chapter 1, meditate at Jason's house before the chapter ends — afterwards the spot is gone.
Keep a manual save from before the end of Chapter 1 as insurance.
Meditate at every remaining spot across Leonida.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bring down one unique animal on a hunt for Bret. GTABase files hunting among Leonida's activities, but the unique-animal contracts are one-off jobs rather than repeatable pastimes: accept the hunt, read the trail clues inside the marked ground, and make the kill cleanly. Any single unique hunt satisfies the trophy — there is no need to clear Bret's whole board.
steps: Meet Bret and accept a unique-animal hunt.
Follow the trail through the marked hunting ground.
Take the animal down and report back to Bret.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Assemble three complete Collectible Card sets. Single cards hide all over the state, which is why this silver lives in the cleanup stage: PowerPyx's collectible route sweeps them region by region once the story is done and every district is open. Think in sets, not loose cards — a set counts only when its final card is in your hand, so finish nearly-complete sets first.
steps: Pocket every card you pass during the story.
After the finale, sweep region by region for the gaps.
Complete any three full sets.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK interaction at 100 different locations. PSNProfiles states the count plainly, and the operative word is locations: returning to a favourite spot advances nothing. Handle it like the stunt total — tag each new spot as your route first crosses it, region by region, and the hundred builds itself long before the cleanup stage arrives.
steps: WAiNK at every new spot you discover.
Work region by region to avoid repeats.
Reach 100 distinct locations.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete any 50 of the game's Challenges — the short scored tasks sprinkled through activities and free roam. Exophase's listing attaches no category condition, so shop for the fifty cheapest: short races, range trials and stunt goals you are already completing for other trophies all feed this same counter, which makes it one of the best-value bronzes in stage IV.
steps: Scan the challenge list and mark the shortest tasks.
Complete challenges alongside your other stage IV work.
Reach 50 completed challenges.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: A partner feat, staged deliberately: with your partner travelling with you, raise a four-star wanted level and then lose it completely, stars draining to zero while the two of you are still together. PowerPyx files these partner trophies as free-roam feats, and the staging is the whole trick — commit the crime somewhere with a fast exit, break line of sight early, and sit hidden until the heat fully dies.
steps: Travel with your partner in free roam.
Raise the wanted level to four stars.
Break pursuit and stay hidden until every star clears.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Chain three shop robberies with your partner while the wanted level never fully drops in between. GTABase's robbery coverage points at the practical shape of it: pick three shops in one neighbourhood, rob the first, and drive straight to the second while still wanted, then the third. If the heat dies mid-chain the count restarts, so on this one speed pays better than the size of the take.
steps: Choose three shops in one neighbourhood; bring your partner.
Rob the first shop and keep the wanted level alive.
Rob the second and third back-to-back without losing the heat.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — get behind the wheel of a hundred different models. PSNProfiles lists it as a discovery count, and ordinary play banks most of it if you steal variety instead of duplicates. The remainder hides where traffic never goes: wealthy districts, marinas and the airport hold parked models seen nowhere else, and one deliberate sweep of those in stage VI finishes the count quickly.
steps: Drive every new model you spot in traffic.
Sweep car parks, marinas and wealthy districts for rare models.
Reach 100 distinct vehicles discovered.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Five takedowns inside a single activation of Combat Focus, the slow-motion combat ability. PowerPyx's feat discipline applies: stage it where enemies cluster — a gang operation or a robbery gone loud — sight all five targets before triggering the ability, and carry a weapon that drops each target in one or two hits so the window is never wasted on a reload.
steps: Find a group of at least five enemies standing close.
Line the group up and activate Combat Focus.
Drop five enemies before the effect ends.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA — the airport. Exophase lists the requirement in exactly those words, and the reading that fits the official text is a free-roam feat rather than a mission: take an aircraft out of the airport without clearance, on your own initiative, outside any scripted sequence. Expect a wanted level for your trouble; the trophy is for the departure itself.
steps: Head to VCIA in free roam.
Take an aircraft without any mission or clearance prompting it.
Get airborne; the trophy registers the departure.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The official description is a wink — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' — and the Rhino is the game's tank, so this feat belongs to time spent in one. GTABase's vehicle and activity coverage is the reference for finding armour in the world: military and high-heat areas are where a Rhino can be taken. Climb in, make the heat the description jokes about, and the stamp follows the feat.
steps: Locate a Rhino tank in free roam.
Take it out and draw serious attention.
Survive the heat the description hints at.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: The quiet counterpart to stage V's loud robberies: rob a jewelry store without being detected, start to finish. PowerPyx's stealth guidance is the shape of it — case the store first, enter when the floor is emptiest, move slowly, and be gone before any alarm state can form. A single detection voids the attempt, but attempts cost nothing: walk away and try the next store.
steps: Choose a jewelry store and watch its routine.
Enter quietly and take the goods without raising detection.
Leave the area still undetected.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: A silver for the robbery line's heavy work: rob five bank vaults and escape after each one. PowerPyx treats vault jobs as the top tier of the robbery activities — bigger preparation, bigger heat — so stage them one at a time with a planned exit route and a fast vehicle waiting. A vault only counts when the escape is completed, not when the vault door opens.
steps: Prepare a vault job: crew, gear, escape vehicle placed.
Crack the vault and take the contents.
Escape the heat; repeat until five vaults are done.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Stop an armoured truck, take its cargo, and escape. GTABase's activity coverage describes these trucks as roaming free-roam targets rather than fixed jobs, so keep an eye out while travelling: block the truck, deal with its guards quickly, breach the rear doors, and be moving again before the response arrives in force. One clean truck satisfies the trophy.
steps: Spot an armoured truck in free roam and block it.
Neutralise the guards and breach the cargo doors.
Take the loot and escape the wanted level.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida — uncover the whole map. PSNProfiles lists it as a pure exploration award, and it completes naturally if your other sweeps are thorough: cards, WAiNK spots, vehicles and strands already drag you into most districts. Whatever fog remains at the end is a stage VI pleasure cruise — drive the untouched corners until the chart is fully inked.
steps: Uncover map regions as your other trophies take you around.
After the finale, identify any still-fogged districts.
Travel through each one until the whole state is explored.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each gang — breadth, not volume: five robberies at five operations of the same gang count once. PowerPyx's robbery route spreads these across stage V, so learn which operation belongs to which gang before you start, tick gangs off as you go, and save the best-defended operation for when your gear is strongest.
steps: Identify one illegal operation per gang.
Rob each gang's operation and escape.
Confirm every gang has been hit exactly once or more.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: One of the atlas's quiet postcards: enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. GTABase's location coverage places the beachfront bars along the Ocean Beach strip; walk in, order the cocktail, and take the moment the description describes. It is a hidden bronze with no fail state — if it does not register, try the neighbouring beachfront bar at a different hour.
steps: Travel to Ocean Beach in free roam.
Enter a beachfront bar with a sea view.
Order and enjoy a cocktail there.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — through the glass, in a car, the way the description's wink intends. Exophase lists it among the hidden free-roam bronzes: enter a showroom, take a vehicle inside it, and exit by driving through the showroom window rather than any door. The style is the requirement; the showroom of your choice is not.
steps: Enter a vehicle showroom in free roam.
Get into one of the display vehicles.
Drive out through the showroom glass.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: A named-place feat: the follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. PSNProfiles carries the official wording verbatim, and the place name is the instruction — travel to that specific alley, play the bowling there, and complete the throw the description calls a follow-through. Other alleys do not substitute for the named one.
steps: Find the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
Start a bowling game there.
Complete the follow-through play at that alley.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The official text is deliberately coy — 'A partnership with mass appeal' — and PowerPyx groups trophies worded like this with the partner feats of stage V: an achievement earned together with your partner, in public, rather than alone. Travel as a pair, work the partner activities and public feats together, and this hidden stamp resolves when the partnership feat it describes is performed.
steps: Travel with your partner in free roam.
Complete partner activities and feats together in public places.
The hidden trophy unlocks when its partnership feat is done.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Another deliberately vague hidden bronze: 'Choices made (for better or worse)'. GTABase's mission coverage is the reference for where the story and strands present real choices; the parenthetical is the reassurance — either branch counts, so this cannot be chosen wrongly. Play naturally, commit to the choices the game offers instead of reloading them, and the stamp lands when the choice it tracks has been made.
steps: Play the story and strands without reloading choices.
Commit to each branching decision when it is offered.
The trophy unlocks once the tracked choice is made.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' — a hidden bronze built around failing once and succeeding on the retry. Exophase lists the wording without conditions, and the shape it describes is forgiving by design: whatever attempt the game counts, the trophy wants the second try, not a flawless first one. If a feat or event goes wrong, run it straight back instead of reloading a save — the retry is the requirement.
steps: Attempt the feat or event the game puts in front of you.
If it fails, retry it immediately rather than reloading.
Succeed on the second attempt.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: The atlas's strangest postcard: the official description only asks 'What the hell just happened?', which marks this as one of the hidden oddity trophies tied to a weird free-roam encounter rather than a listed task. PSNProfiles carries it among the hidden bronzes. The practical route is exploration itself — strange markers, odd strangers and unexplained events in remote corners are where trophies worded like this live; investigate them instead of driving past.
steps: Explore remote corners and follow strange markers.
Investigate odd encounters instead of skipping them.
The hidden trophy unlocks at the encounter it describes.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: A bowling joke with a body count: bowl pedestrians over with a melee drive-by — striking them from a moving vehicle with a melee attack rather than the vehicle itself. PowerPyx files feats like this under deliberate staging: find a tight group on a pavement, take a slow pass on a bike or in an open vehicle, and swing as you pass. One clean pass that connects is the whole trophy.
steps: Find a group of pedestrians on a pavement.
Ride or drive past them slowly.
Land a melee strike from the vehicle as you pass.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder marked bills through your contacts until the laundered total reaches $250,000. GTABase's economy coverage is the reference for where marked bills come from — the robbery line of stage V is the natural supply — so feed every marked haul into the laundering contacts instead of spending it raw. It is a cumulative counter: no single run needs to be large, but the habit must start early.
steps: Collect marked bills from robberies and jobs.
Hand them to your laundering contacts rather than spending them.
Reach $250,000 laundered in total.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — cumulative, and across the shop network rather than in one spree. Exophase's wording matches the official text exactly. Ordinary outfitting covers much of it if you buy rather than steal your gear; the stage VI remainder is painless once the robbery and laundering income is flowing, so finish it with the vehicles, clothing and equipment you wanted anyway.
steps: Buy gear, clothing and services from shops as you play.
Keep expensive purchases in shops rather than elsewhere.
Reach $100,000 spent in total.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property on the market. PowerPyx places property completion in the cleanup stage for a simple reason: the full set costs more than the story alone pays, so let the stage V robberies and stage VI laundering fill the account first. Buy garages as they become affordable, cheapest first, and the trophy lands with the final deed.
steps: Note every garage property as it comes on the market.
Build income through robberies and laundering.
Purchase all garage properties.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the last stamp on the chart for most travellers. PSNProfiles lists the count plainly, and it pairs naturally with Whip It Good: every new vehicle you discover is a candidate for registration, so register as you discover instead of saving the paperwork for the end. Ten registrations close the atlas's final page.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app when you acquire a vehicle.
Register each new vehicle as you go.
Reach 10 registered vehicles.
